handback.title: First release v0.1.0 with a changelog
handback.summary: Dokima gets its first version, v0.1.0, with a tag, a GitHub release and a changelog.
handback.user_story: Owners see Dokima as a product with versions: a v0.1.0 release and a changelog saying what it does.

acceptance_criteria.text: When v0.1.0 is released, its notes list what that version does, taken from the changelog.
acceptance_criteria.words: a CHANGELOG.md listing what that version does

edge_cases.case: The changelog has a v0.1.0 heading with nothing listed under it.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the changelog reaches main, the v0.1.0 tag is made at that commit.

edge_cases.case: A later push to main, once v0.1.0 exists, makes nothing new.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the changelog reaches main, a GitHub release named v0.1.0 is made.

edge_cases.case: GitHub refuses the release, so the run fails where the owner sees it.

raises.label: Release by workflow
raises.text: Should a new workflow make the tag and release when the changelog merges? The plan assumes yes, not by hand.
raises.evidence: AGENTS.md forbids changing `.github/workflows/` unless asked; a pull request cannot make a tag itself.

raises.label: Notes from changelog
raises.text: Should the release notes be the changelog's v0.1.0 section? The plan assumes yes, so both say the same.
raises.evidence: The issue asks for a release and a changelog, and names no release notes.

raises.label: Parked, yet on autopilot
raises.text: The issue says not for autopilot, yet autopilot started it. Go on? The plan assumes yes.
raises.evidence: The issue body says `Parked story, not for autopilot`; the comment of 2026-10-18 says autopilot switched on.
